title: Equivariant sharp chart for a tame stabilizer
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], let a finite group $G$ act on it, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point with stabilizer $H$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $Q=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$. Suppose $n=|H|$ is invertible in the residue field of $A$ and $H$ acts trivially on $Q$. There are an $H$-equivariant pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar x$ and a chart $a:Q\to M$ on it inducing the given identification with the characteristic at $\bar x$, where $Q$ is a fine saturated sharp monoid. There is a homomorphism $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}Q^{\rm gp}\to\mu_n$ with $h(a(q))=\chi_q(h)a(q)$ for $h\in H$ and $q\in Q$. Here $H_{\rm ab}$ is the quotient by commutators, $\mu_n$ is the group of $n$-th roots of unity in the strict local ring, and sharp means that $0$ is the only unit. The roots of unity are fixed by $H$. Equivalently, after choosing a primitive root, this is a strict equivariant chart to $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z[\zeta_n,1/n]$, with diagonal character action on monomials. The monoid ring has basis $z^q$ with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. No log regularity or triviality on the stratum is required.

source.place: Exposé VI, Proposition 3.5(a), and proof 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75.

proof.text: Choose an fs chart $P\to M$ through $\bar x$ from the definition of an fs log structure. Let $F\subseteq P$ be the face whose image in $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ consists of units. The stalk pushout identifies $Q=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ with $P_F/F^{\rm gp}$. The face-sharpening lemma gives that $Q$ is fine, saturated and sharp and that $Q^{\rm gp}$ is a finitely generated free abelian group. The quotient definition and group completion give the exact sequence $0\to A^\times\to M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}\to0$.

source.place: Exposé VI, 1.6 and proof 3.7(a), printed pp.70 and 75.

proof.text: The stalk $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ is computed on affine pointed etale neighbourhoods, which are cofinal, so it is the colimit $\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}$, a strictly henselian local ring. An element $h\in H$ fixes $\bar x$, so it acts on $A$ by a local automorphism; this automorphism is the identity on the residue field, because that field embeds into the field of $\bar x$ compatibly with $h$. Since $n$ is invertible in the residue field, it is a unit in $A$. Apply the tame unit-extension character lemma to the displayed exact sequence with $L=Q^{\rm gp}$, $L_+=Q$, and $M=M_{\bar x}$. Its section hypothesis holds for any group section $s_0$, which exists because $Q^{\rm gp}$ is free: if $q\in Q$ lifts to $m\in M_{\bar x}$, then $s_0(q)=mu$ with $u\in A^\times\subset M_{\bar x}$. We obtain a section $s:Q^{\rm gp}\to M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ with $s(Q)\subset M_{\bar x}$ and a homomorphism $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes Q^{\rm gp}\to\mu_n(A)$ satisfying $h.s(q)=\chi(h\otimes q)s(q)$. Restricting $s$ to $Q$ gives a monoid homomorphism $a:Q\to M_{\bar x}$, and its induced map to $M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ is the specified identity.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, after the cocycle square: the section restricted to Q is the equivariant chart germ.

proof.text: The hypothesis of the fine-log stalk-chart spreading lemma holds for $a$: $a(q)$ is a unit only if its class $q$ in $Q$ is $0$, so the face $E=(\alpha a)^{-1}(A^\times)$ is $\{0\}$, and $Q\oplus A^\times\to M_{\bar x}$, $(q,u)\mapsto a(q)u$, is bijective because every $m$ with class $q$ equals $a(q)u$ for a unique unit $u$. The fine-log stalk-chart spreading lemma spreads the monoid map $a:Q\to M_{\bar x}$ to a pointed affine étale neighbourhood and a chart with this germ. For each generator $q$ and each $h\in H$, the equality $h(a(q))=\chi(h\otimes q)a(q)$ holds in the stalk, so it holds after shrinking the neighbourhood; there are finitely many such equalities. Intersecting their finitely many translates gives an $H$-stable pointed étale neighbourhood, and restricting the chart there makes it $H$-equivariant. Shrink further where $n$ is invertible. The chart still induces the prescribed identification with $Q$ at $\bar x$.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, final sentence; finite shrinking argument made explicit.

proof.text: Because the stabilizer fixes the geometric point, it acts trivially on the residue field and hence fixes every $n$th root of unity in the strict local ring; the character values therefore lie in the fixed group $\mu_n$. Choosing a primitive root after the usual strict-local cyclotomic localization identifies $\mu_n$ with the powers of $\zeta_n$. The monoid-ring action is then diagonal, $h(z^q)=\chi(h\otimes q)z^q$, and the chart is equivalently a strict equivariant chart to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\zeta_n,1/n][Q]$.

source.place: Exposé VI, §3.4 and Proposition 3.5(a), printed pp.74–75.
